title: What are Type Aliases?
overview: Type aliases allow developers to create custom names for existing types. They help make complex types easier to read and reuse.

example.title: Type Alias Example
example.content:
type Username = string;

let name: Username = 'Manthan';

title: Creating Object Type Aliases
overview: Type aliases can define the structure of objects similar to interfaces. They are useful for creating reusable object types.

example.title: Object Type Alias

title: Type Aliases with Arrays
overview: Type aliases can be used to define custom array types, making repeated array type declarations simpler.

example.title: Array Type Alias
example.content:
type Numbers = number[];

const values: Numbers = [1,2,3];

title: Type Aliases with Union Types
overview: Type aliases can combine multiple types using union operators. This allows a value to accept more than one type.

title: Interface vs Type Alias
overview: Interfaces and type aliases both define custom types, but they have different capabilities. Interfaces are commonly used for objects, while type aliases are more flexible.

example.title: Comparison
example.content:
Interface:
• Mainly used for object structures.

Type Alias:
• Supports objects, unions, primitives, and more.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how to create reusable custom types using type aliases, define objects and arrays, use unions, and understand the difference between interfaces and type aliases.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
